title: Zero Displacement? Position Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A lift goes up three floors and comes back down. A swimmer swims one length and back. Aarav rides 200 m to the shop and rides home. His wheels rolled 400 m, yet his displacement is zero. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn what position and displacement mean, and why displacement can be zero.

We run the ride on a live motion notebook: the bicycle, a violet displacement arrow that grows and shrinks, a path counter and a position-time graph moving together, with a slow-mo replay. We reason it out link by link, derive delta x = x2 - x1 step by step with a units check, compare home to shop and shop to home side by side, test what happens when you move the origin, then solve a corridor worked example, the exam trap about the sign, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Back home, moved how far?
0:30 Position: distance from the origin, with a sign
0:53 The ride: displacement arrow vs path (live sim + graph)
1:33 Why the displacement is zero
1:52 The rule: delta x = x2 - x1, step by step
2:33 Side by side + pause and think
3:08 Move the origin: does displacement change?
3:34 Worked example: the college corridor
4:14 Exam trap: keep the sign
4:39 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:17 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Distance and Displacement. One lap of a 400 m track: distance 400 m, displacement zero. Can the two ever be equal?
